parsed.attack: A self-taught Hungarian learner has a finite verb list, and the hundred or so verbs that carry ordinary speech get shared out of Safari in the first weekend - this is a product used hard for four days and then never again, because nobody re-conjugates a verb they already have a deck for. The claimed moat, accumulated_personal_corpus, cannot form here by construction: the deck is exported into the learner's drill app on the first run, so what accumulates belongs to Anki and this product keeps nothing. That leaves the shareable-artifact loop, which needs people still using it in month three to post decks, and by month three the only users in existence are new installs.
parsed.strongest_defence: It is a one-time purchase, so the 57.9% first-renewal battle is not being fought at all - a tool used flat out for one weekend and then left idle is the normal shape of a utility purchase, and utilities are the category that does retain and does get repurchased. The right comparison is a file converter, not a subscription: the buyer got exactly what they paid for, and growth comes from Finnish, Estonian and Turkish rather than from re-engaging the Hungarian buyer.
parsed.verdict_reason: One-time pricing genuinely removes the renewal battle, but the corpus moat cannot form when the artifact is exported on first use, and the distribution loop depends on users who will have stopped by week three.
